correctness.rationale: For compactly supported invariant \(\mu\), testing the generator against arbitrary functions of \(z\) proves \(\mathbb E[dxy-mz\mid z]=0\). Exact identities for \(L(x^2)\) and \(L(z^2)\) give \(\mathbb E[(z+1/(2b))^2]=1/(4b^2)+(ad/(bm))\mathbb E[x^2]\). If equality holds, support lies in \(x=0\); a complete compact trajectory there has \(\dot z=-mz\), forcing \(z=0\), then \(y=0\). The slab obstruction follows because the completed square is pointwise at most \(1/(4b^2)\) on \(-1/b\le z\le0\). The packaged exact-arithmetic checker replays the critical polynomial certificate.

value.rationale: The natural interval \([-1/b,0]\) is selected by the roots of the exact quadratic height expression \(z(1+bz)\), not by an arbitrary numerical slice. The theorem converts local polynomial dynamics into a global constraint on every compact recurrent statistical state, independent of scroll count and of the parameter \(c\). The equality case is completely rigid, so the defect yields a concrete recurrence obstruction for all nontrivial periodic, quasiperiodic, or chaotic compact components. This is structurally informative beyond recomputing known equilibria or a single simulated attractor.
